explain: The first load to line 3 misses, takes MSHR 0 and raises mem_req. Every later load to line 3 finds MSHR 0 and merges as a secondary miss: mem_req stays low and secondary_misses counts up. Without fills, the line never arrives, but the cache does not stall.

Lines 3 and 5 take both MSHRs. The load to line 7 misses with no MSHR free and no match, so ld_ready drops. Loads to 3 or 5 are still taken because they merge. A non-blocking cache with two MSHRs tolerates two outstanding misses.
